findings.title: Legacy saves overwrite scoring state and duplicate relabeled answers
findings.problem: The legacy-write branch preserves only old.blob.log, while accepting the incoming snapshot's XP, ability, streak, schedules, and rewards wholesale. Its log deduplication also compares entire JSON objects, so a pre-migration answer does not match the same answer after migration 020 adds source, key, and unclassified fields.
findings.failure_scenario: A browser opened before deployment has one unscoped answer. Migration 020 relabels that answer, and another device subsequently saves additional work. The old browser then autosaves. This trigger appends its original unscoped answer as a duplicate, rolls ability and XP back to the old snapshot, and can remove the new rewards and review dates. The persisted answer count and ability no longer describe the same history.
findings.fix: Do not accept a legacy whole-blob replacement while preserving only its log. Either retire legacy writers safely or reconcile the complete state server-side using occurrence-aware answer matching. Add a database-level regression test that runs the relabel migration, saves newer progress, then submits a pre-change upsert and checks history, XP, ability, rewards, and schedules.

findings.title: Normal autosaves rebuild protected streaks without their earned covers
findings.problem: reconcileProgress calls streakBeforeInsertedDay whenever there is an unseen attempt. That helper tests whether any activity predates the baseline's last day—not whether the incoming activity does—and rebuilds the streak using emptyRewards(). It neither restores consumed covers nor replays their grants. Consequently, even an ordinary chronological answer can replace a valid cover-protected streak with a shorter streak and a different shield state.
findings.failure_scenario: An account uses its shield and one banked cover to bridge Tuesday and Wednesday between Monday and Thursday study. Its saved streak is count 2, lastDay Thursday, shield false. After Friday's answer, the live calculation correctly produces count 3. The normal blobForSave reconciliation rebuilds Monday–Thursday–Friday with zero covers, restarts on Thursday, and saves count 2 with the shield ready instead.
findings.fix: Keep the baseline streak for chronological additions. If historical insertion requires reconstruction, replay the actual shield/cover history rather than starting with emptyRewards(). Add a regression covering an ordinary save after a gap protected by both a shield and a cover, asserting both count and shield.

findings.title: Explicit sign-in routes still lose to the preserved signup flag
findings.problem: authModeFromUrl gives ?start=1 precedence over APP_SIGN_IN. The new trial navigation preserves the current query string when switching to sign-in, so it creates URLs whose displayed mode changes after a reload.
findings.failure_scenario: A visitor enters /app/?start=1, selects Try questions, then selects I have an account. AuthGate displays sign-in at /app/sign-in?start=1. Reloading that page calls authModeFromUrl and opens signup instead of sign-in.
findings.fix: Give explicit auth paths precedence over the legacy start flag, or remove start when navigating to an explicit auth mode. Add a regression for the complete signup-link → trial → sign-in → reload sequence.

assessment: Not safe to release. Legacy-client saves can corrupt answer history and ability, and ordinary autosaves can undo cover-protected streaks. The trial-to-sign-in flow also reloads into the wrong auth mode. These findings are based on the supplied code; tests were not executed.
